main_text.p: cabor de inimicis meis. Conuerta manum meã super te, & repurgabo quàm purè scoriam tuã,& auferá omne stannũ tuum.Re-stituáq; iudices tuos sicut à principio, & cõsiliarios tuos sicut ab initio, & postea dicetur de te: Civitas est iusticiæ, & urbs fidelis. Zion in iudicio redimetur, reverten-turq; ad eam in iusticia. Contritio autẽ ini-quorum & peccatorum pariter fiet, & desertores Domini confumentur. Quoniam confundentur propter deos, quos habere desiderastis, & ignominia afficiemini propter hortos (lucorum) quos elegistis. Quoniá eritis sicut arbor cuius folium mar-cescit, & sicut hortus qui nõ habet aquas. Eritq; fortitudo(sculptilis vestri)sicut stup-pa,& fabricator eius quasi scintilla,& comburentur ambo ipsi simul, nec erit qui ex-tinguere possit.
main_text.head: ANNOTATIONES.
main_text.p: AUdite cœli, & adverte terra, quoniâ, &c.) Hæc est prima pars clarissimi huius Ope-ris,continens visiones seu prædictiones,& con-ciones habitas à propheta sub rege Uzia, qui & pri-mus [?]in

page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment ("cabor") and is kept as such. "scoriam" read from "fco riam" (long s looks like f). Line-end hyphens kept as printed (Re-, ini-, dice-, de-, habe-, reuerten-, mar-, ex-, stup-, Ope-, con-, pri-). "comburentur" has no visible hyphen at the line end and is written whole. The final word "in" on the last line is hard to read in the italic and is marked [?]. The drop cap A is joined to "Udite" as "AUdite". The italic lines are Hæc est... through pri-mus in.
